t:
That 

    (a) 
there is established a Towing Safety Advisory Committee (hereinafter referred to as the “Committee”). The Committee shall consist of sixteen members with particular expertise, knowledge, and experience regarding shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety as follows:

        (1) 
seven members from the barge and towing industry, reflecting a regional geographic balance;
 
        (2) 
one member from the offshore mineral and oil supply vessel industry; and
 
        (3) 
two members from each of the following—

            (A) 
port districts, authorities, or terminal operators;
 
            (B) 
maritime labor;
 
            (C) 
shippers (of whom at least one shall be engaged in the shipment of oil or hazardous materials by barge); and
 
            (D) 
the general public.
   
    (b) 
The Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating (hereinafter referred to as the “Secretary”) shall appoint the members of the Committee. The Secretary shall designate one of the members of the Committee as the Chairman and one of the members as the Vice Chairman. The Vice Chairman shall act as Chairman in the absence or incapacity of, or in the event of a vacancy in the office of, the Chairman. The Secretary may request the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of Commerce to each designate a representative to participate as an observer on the Committee.
 
    (c) 
The Committee shall advise, consult with, and make recommendations to the Secretary on matters relating to shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety. Any advice or recommendation made by the Committee to the Secretary shall reflect the independent judgment of the Committee on the matter concerned. The Secretary shall consult with the Committee before taking any significant action affecting shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety. The Committee shall meet at the call of the Secretary, but in any event not less than once during each calendar year. All proceedings of the Committee shall be open to the public, and a record of the proceedings shall be made available for public inspection.
 
    (d) The Secretary shall furnish to the Committee an executive secretary and such secretarial, clerical, and other services as are considered necessary for the conduct of its business. There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to implement the provisions of this subsection.
 
    (e) Unless extended by subsequent Act of Congress, the Committee shall terminate five years from the date of enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The section creates an advisory committee whose members come from industry, maritime labor, shippers, port authorities and the general public, all outside the federal government, and it requires the Secretary to consult that committee before taking significant action. The tempting 'No' reading is that the Secretary appoints the members and other federal Secretaries may designate observers, making it look intra-governmental. That fails because the voting membership is non-federal and its proceedings are open to the public.
fable.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Committee before taking any significant action affecting shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety.

qwen_block.w: The section establishes a Towing Safety Advisory Committee composed of non-federal members, including industry representatives, labor unions, and the general public. It explicitly requires the Secretary to consult with this committee before taking significant actions, which constitutes participation by outside parties in federal decision-making.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Committee before taking any significant action affecting shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety.

opus.w: The section sets up an advisory committee made of non-federal members, including the barge and towing industry, maritime labor, shippers, port authorities and the general public. It requires the Secretary to consult the committee before taking any significant action on towing safety, and its proceedings are open to the public. The federal observers from the Army and Commerce do not make this an intra-government process, because the voting members are outsiders who take part in federal decisions.
opus.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Committee before taking any significant action affecting shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety.
opus.b: This is clearly a "Yes." The tempting wrong reading would be to treat the Army and Commerce observers as making this an intra-government arrangement. That fails because the 16 voting members come from outside the government: industry, labor, shippers, port authorities, and the general public. The Secretary must also consult this committee before acting.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes an advisory committee composed of non-federal entities, including industry representatives, labor unions, shippers, and the general public. The statute explicitly requires the Secretary to consult with this committee before taking significant actions, which fits the definition of participation involving outside parties in federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: The Committee shall consist of sixteen members... seven members from the barge and towing industry... two members from each of the following... maritime labor... shippers... and the general public... The Secretary shall consult with the Committee before taking any significant action affecting shallow-draft inland and coastal waterway navigation and towing safety.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "No" because the Secretary appoints the members, implying they are federal employees or that the committee is purely internal. However, the definition explicitly states that advisory committees with non-federal members (e.g., industry, labor, public) constitute participation. The text clearly lists members from the "barge and towing industry," "maritime labor," "shippers," and the "general public," who are outside the federal government. The requirement that the Secretary "consult with the Committee before taking any significant action" confirms this is participation in a federal decision.
